I found two problems in the diff. The first I confirmed by reading the parser code; the second is likely but not certain. I couldn't run either scenario, because writing test files to `/tmp` was denied, so both come from reading the code.

1. **Parser crash on a side-effect `@import`** (confirmed), at `/work/repo/microsoft__typescript-go/internal/parser/reparser.go:120`. For `/** @import "./types" */` the parser leaves `ImportClause` empty (nil). The new reparse code then calls `importTag.ImportClause.Clone(&p.factory)` with no nil check, and the parser panics. That would crash tsgo or the language server on any JS file containing such a tag; the old tag-based code handled it. No existing test uses this form. The fix is to skip the clone (or the whole reparse) when `ImportClause` is nil.

2. **`@import` on a nested node is no longer resolved** (plausible), at `/work/repo/microsoft__typescript-go/internal/ast/utilities.go:2556`. The PR removes the tag-handling branch from `ForEachDynamicImportOrRequireCall`, which used to find `@import` tags anywhere in the file. Now the only record is the new synthetic import node, and it goes into whichever list the parser is building at that moment. For an `@import` inside a function body or class, that's the body or member list, not the top level. `collectModuleReferences` only scans top-level statements, so the module is never added to `file.Imports` and never resolved. `checkImportDeclaration` also reports a new, wrong error: "An import declaration can only be used at the top level of a module". TypeScript allows `@import` anywhere.

- internal/parser/reparser.go:120 — nil `ImportClause` is cloned for a side-effect `@import "mod"` tag, so the parser panics.
- internal/ast/utilities.go:2556 — nested `@import` tags are no longer collected into `file.Imports`, and they now trigger a false top-level-import error.
